title: weave-attn: chunked fused-attention kernel + windowed KV caching + continuous-batcher
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduces a new fused chunked-attention kernel (weave-attn) with windowed KV caching and a continuous-batcher micro-scheduler. Improves throughput for long-context workloads and reduces P99 latency for small requests; includes opt-in rollout and compatibility shim for pinned models.
description:
Context and motivation:
We see two recurring pain points in production: (1) long-context generation workloads suffer from high memory pressure and degraded throughput due to monolithic KV cache handling, and (2) mixed small/large request workloads cause suboptimal batching decisions that harm latency-sensitive routes. This PR introduces a combined runtime change targeted at those two areas: a fused, chunked attention kernel ("weave-attn") that processes attention in contiguous chunks to improve memory locality and vectorization, plus a windowed KV caching layer that shards and trims KV state by logical token windows, and a continuous-batcher micro-scheduler that keeps the GPU feeding while preserving latency SLOs for small requests.

Design summary (high level):
- Fused chunked-attention kernel (runtime/attention/weave_kernel.*): implements a tiled attention path that accepts a per-request chunking strategy. For short sequences the kernel uses an in-register fastpath; for long sequences it streams chunks with overlap to maintain rotary/rope alignment. The kernel is written in CUDA with a CPU fallback and a compact C++ dispatch shim.
- Windowed KV cache (runtime/kv/windowed_cache.*): KV state is partitioned into fixed-size windows (configurable per-model). When sequence windows age out, the cache drops the oldest window instead of evicting by token-trace alone, which reduces cache churn for streaming decodes. The cache exposes a backward-compatible interface so existing scheduler logic can opt into windowed mode per-model.
- Continuous-batcher micro-scheduler (runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.*): a lightweight scheduler that keeps warm batches on a small timer and opportunistically merges tolerant small requests while respecting per-route latency budgets. Integrates with existing autoscaling/batching knobs and supports per-tenant configuration.

Commits (summary):
1) feat(attn): implement weave-attn fused chunked kernel (add CUDA + unit tests)
2) feat(kv): windowed KV cache implementation + integration tests
3) feat(scheduler): continuous-batcher scheduler + metrics/tracing hooks
4) perf: integration benchmark harness and batch shape simulator (bench/perf/weave_attn_bench.py)
5) docs: operator and rollout guide, API compatibility notes
6) test: add regression tests for rotary alignment across chunk boundaries

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/attention/weave_kernel.cu, weave_kernel.h, weave_dispatch.cpp
- runtime/kv/windowed_cache.h, windowed_cache.cpp, windowed_cache_test.cc
- runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp, continuous_batcher.h, continuous_batcher_test.cc
- bench/perf/weave_attn_bench.py
- docs/operators/weave-attn-rollout.md
- sdk/python/redwood/rollouts.py (opt-in flag)
- tests/regressions/rotary_chunk_alignment.py
- ci/workflows/gpu-smoke.yml (added new perf job)

Benchmarks (representative, measured on p4d):
- Long-context throughput (32k tokens, batch=1): weave-attn end-to-end TP increases 1.8x versus baseline tiled kernel; GPU memory peak reduced ~15%.
- Mixed small/large request steady-state: continuous-batcher improves small-request P99 by 18% at 95th percentile load while maintaining >90% of baseline throughput for long requests.
- Prefix-heavy streaming workloads: windowed KV cache reduces KV write amplification and lowers token cost by ~12% on average for our synthetic newsroom workload.
Notes: absolute numbers vary by model and sequence distribution; included bench harness for reproducibility.

Compatibility and rollout:
- The new kernel and cache are behind feature flags. Models can opt-in via model config: pipelineOptions.kernel = "weave" and kv.cache_mode = "windowed". The SDK exposes an opt-in helper to mark routes for continuous-batcher.
- Backward compatible: default behavior remains unchanged until rollout is enabled. We provide a compatibility shim that translates existing KV pointers to the windowed layout for mixed nodes during rollout.

Testing and CI:
- Added unit and integration tests that validate rotary/rope index continuity across chunk boundaries and cross-node migration for cached windows.
- CI matrix includes gpu-smoke (new), cpu-unit, integration, and flake8/lint. First CI run hit a nondeterministic race in the batcher timer (GPU smoke failed intermittently); fixed by introducing a scoped wakeup token and retry logic. Final CI status: pass across matrix.

Review thread (highlights):
- Miguel: "Nice work on the chunked kernel — can you explain how we preserve rotary index offsets when we stream overlapping chunks?"
- Author (Ava): "We implemented an index remap layer inside weave_dispatch.cpp that carries per-request base offsets and applies an incremental offset when emitting kv slices; tests included to validate wrap-around cases."
- Priya: "Concern: continuous-batcher may increase tail latency for very low-concurrency tenants. Can we add a tenant-level opt-out?"
- Author: "Added per-tenant gating and a rate-based quick-path that bypasses batching for latency-critical tenants; added docs and tests."
- Daniel: "Please add a rollout plan and kill-switch for autoscaling regression. Also request to surface metrics for window eviction rate."
- Author: "Added rollout doc with kill-switch and added window_evictions/sec and evicted_window_age histograms to the metrics surface."
- Approval: Miguel and Priya approved after fixes; Daniel did final approval with minor nits addressed.

CI details and troubleshooting:
- Initial lint failure due to formatting in weave_dispatch.cpp (fixed).
- Intermittent GPU smoke failure due to batcher timer race; repro in bench harness, fix landed in commit 3.
- Final CI: all checks green (unit/integration/gpu-smoke/perf bench runs).

Merge and release notes:
- Merge method: squash and merge to main. Merge commit: 0f3b7c9 (squash)
- Merged by: Miguel Torres on 2026-03-09
- Release note (operators): Opt-in kernel 'weave' and 'windowed' KV cache. Expect throughput gains for long-context workloads and lower memory usage; monitor window_evictions and batcher_queue_latency.

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Investigate a hybrid eviction policy that is size-aware inside windows (ENG-9124).
- Add adaptive window sizing based on request distribution (ENG-9150).
- Port a subset of microbenchmarks to the on-prem installer to validate behavior in Private deployments.

Author's testing checklist (from PR body):
- [x] Unit tests for kernel numeric equivalence on fp16/fp32 paths

Summary: This PR is a performance-oriented change set that combines kernel-level improvements with cache and scheduler enhancements to address real production pain points. It is feature-flagged, tested, and merged with a controlled rollout plan.
